1.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/audits/uses-rel-preconnect.js is the heart of the audit that scans only network records (devtools logs) for DNS+TCP timing. It never reads the page’s DOM to check for existing <link rel=preconnect|dns-prefetch> hints, so it always reports savings even when hints are present.  
• lighthouse-core/lib/element.js is the helper library used by other audits to query DOM nodes; to extend uses-rel-preconnect to inspect <link> tags you’d use element.js to locate those hints in the document.  
• lighthouse-core/gather/gatherers/html-without-javascript.js is the gatherer that returns the page’s static HTML. You’d update the audit to depend on this artifact (or introduce a new link-elements gatherer) so it can parse out existing preconnect/dns-prefetch link tags before computing savings.
1.bug_scenario: When you run Lighthouse’s “Avoid multiple, costly round trips to any origin” (uses-rel-preconnect) audit against a page that already includes <link rel="preconnect"> (or dns-prefetch) hints for the same origins, Lighthouse still flags those origins as opportunities. In other words, the audit is blind to preconnect hints already present in the DOM and reports a false positive.

2.explanation: 1. uses-rel-preconnect.js is the heart of the audit logic. It only analyzes networkRecords from DevTools and computes which origins could benefit from preconnect, but never checks the DOM for existing <link rel=preconnect> or dns-prefetch hints. 2. default-config.js must be updated so that if we introduce an artifact (e.g. a LinkElements gatherer) to surface <link rel> tags from the page, that gatherer is actually wired up in the config. Without adding the gatherer to default-config, artifacts.LinkElements will be empty and the audit won’t be able to detect existing hints.
2.bug_scenario: When you run Lighthouse (v3.0.3) on a page that already includes <link rel="preconnect"> or dns-prefetch hints for certain third-party origins (e.g. Google Analytics or Google Fonts), the “Avoid multiple, costly round trips to any origin” opportunity (uses-rel-preconnect audit) still reports those same origins as if no preconnect hints exist. In short, the audit only inspects network records and never looks at the page’s DOM for existing <link rel="preconnect"|"dns-prefetch"> tags, so it produces a false positive.
